title: Removing one top-dimensional nondegenerate simplex
statement:
Let $A$ be a simplicial set with finitely many nondegenerate simplices, in the conventions of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Let $d\geq0$ and assume every nondegenerate simplex of $A$ has dimension at most $d$. Choose a nondegenerate simplex $\sigma\in A_d$. For each $m\geq0$ define
$$U_m=A_m\setminus\{A(\alpha)(\sigma)\mid\alpha:[m]\twoheadrightarrow[d]\text{ is order preserving}\}.$$
Then the $U_m$, with the operators restricted from $A$, form a simplicial subset $U\subseteq A$. Under this inclusion the nondegenerate simplices of $U$ are exactly the nondegenerate simplices of $A$ other than $\sigma$. In particular $U$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices, all of dimension at most $d$, and one fewer nondegenerate $d$-simplex than $A$. Moreover $U_m=A_m$ for $m<d$, $A_d=U_d\amalg\{\sigma\}$, and every simplex of $A_m\setminus U_m$ for $m>d$ is degenerate in $A$. The case $d=0$ and the possibility $U=\varnothing$ are included.
